answer: An acoustic channel-sounding protocol curbs Sybil attacks in an agent economy monitoring a coral reef. Verifiers emit ultrasonic pings through copper hydrophones, mapping spatial multipath signatures unique to each node's physical position. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of deploying dedicated marine hardware per identity rather than simulating virtual peers. However, water turbulence and saffron algae blooms distort acoustic propagation, causing false rejections.
